extracted.intended_audience: reinforcement-learning researchers and ML practitioners preparing papers/experiments (NeurIPS/ICML/ICLR authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and checklist for making reinforcement-learning research reproducible, reusable, and robust — aimed at authors reporting algorithms, theoretical claims, and empirical results. Emphasizes reporting of code, hyperparameters, experimental procedure, statistics, and generalization evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Reproducibility refers to the ability of a researcher to duplicate the results of a prior study….”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproducibility is presented as a minimum necessary condition for a finding to be believable and informative (Bollen et al., NSF 2015).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reusability (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Using the same materials as were used by the original investigator.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reusability is identified alongside reproducibility and robustness as a desirable property of scientific artifacts (e.g., datasets, code, environments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness (definition/practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Robustness — ability of results/methods to hold under variations and perturbations (e.g., different hyperparameters, seeds, environments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slides motivate robustness via sensitivity of RL methods to hyperparameters, codebase differences, and environment perturbations; stress moving from fair comparisons to robust conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check: clear description of the algorithm
rubrics_metrics.description: For all algorithms presented, check if you include: A clear description of the algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide enough detail that others can understand the algorithmic procedure without relying solely on code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check: analysis of complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: For all algorithms presented, check if you include: An analysis of the complexity (time, space, sample size) of the algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify computational and sample complexity to enable fair comparison and reproducibility under resource constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check: link to downloadable source code and dependencies
rubrics_metrics.description: For all algorithms presented, check if you include: A link to downloadable source code, including all dependencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete code + dependency specification (versions, environment) so others can run the same experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical claims: statement and assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: For any theoretical claim, check if you include: A statement of the result; A clear explanation of any assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the theorem/claim precisely and list all assumptions required for the result to hold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical claims: proof
rubrics_metrics.description: For any theoretical claim, check if you include: A complete proof of the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full proofs (or clearly referenced appendices) so results can be independently verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical reporting: description of data collection and sample size
rubrics_metrics.description: For all figures and tables that present empirical results, check if you include: A complete description of the data collection process, including sample size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how data/trajectories/episodes were collected and report sample sizes for transparency and replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical reporting: link to dataset or simulation environment
rubrics_metrics.description: For all figures and tables that present empirical results, check if you include: A link to downloadable version of the dataset or simulation environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide access to the exact dataset or simulator version used (or seed/configuration) to allow replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical reporting: train/validation/test allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: For all figures and tables that present empirical results, check if you include: An explanation of how sample were allocated for training / validation / testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit the procedure used to split data or tasks and whether evaluation uses held-out tasks/environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical reporting: excluded data
rubrics_metrics.description: For all figures and tables that present empirical results, check if you include: An explanation of any data that was excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report any exclusions and the rationale (e.g., filtering failed runs) to avoid undisclosed selection bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical reporting: hyperparameter search and specification
rubrics_metrics.description: For all figures and tables that present empirical results, check if you include: The range of hyper-parameters considered, the method to select the best hyper-parameter configuration, and specification of all hyper-parameters used to generate results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List search ranges, optimization/selection procedure (e.g., grid/random/search budget), and the final hyperparameters used for both proposed method and baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical reporting: exact number of evaluation runs
rubrics_metrics.description: For all figures and tables that present empirical results, check if you include: The exact number of evaluation runs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the number of independent seeds/trials used per reported data point so variability and statistical power are clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical reporting: description of how experiments were run
rubrics_metrics.description: For all figures and tables that present empirical results, check if you include: A description of how experiments were run.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include run scripts, order of experiments, parallelization, and any non-obvious orchestration details that affect results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical reporting: definition of measures/statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: For all figures and tables that present empirical results, check if you include: A clear definition of the specific measure or statistics used to report results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define metrics (e.g., return, normalized score), aggregation method (per-episode, per-step), and any post-processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical reporting: error bars
rubrics_metrics.description: For all figures and tables that present empirical results, check if you include: Clearly defined error bars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify what error bars represent (stddev, standard error, confidence interval) and how they were computed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical reporting: central tendency and variation
rubrics_metrics.description: For all figures and tables that present empirical results, check if you include: A description of results including central tendency (e.g. mean) and variation (e.g. stddev).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both mean/median and an appropriate measure of dispersion to convey reliability of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical reporting: computing infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: For all figures and tables that present empirical results, check if you include: The computing infrastructure used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report hardware/GPUs, parallelization, and runtimes so others can reproduce compute budget and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair comparisons: equal data and compute
rubrics_metrics.description: Fair comparison is easy, right? Same amount of data. Same amount of computation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure baselines are given comparable data and compute budgets; document any differences in training time or compute resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measurement and trial selection
rubrics_metrics.description: How should we measure performance of the learned policy? (Average return over test trials? Confidence interval? How do we pick n?)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose appropriate performance measures, report confidence intervals, and justify the number of runs (n) used for reporting and statistical testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperparameter tuning fairness and sensitivity analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Different methods have distinct sets of hyperparameters and exhibit variable sensitivity to hyperparams. What method is best often depends on data/compute budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report hyperparameter sensitivity analyses and ensure tuning effort is comparable across methods; consider showing performance across budgets/searches rather than only best-tuned numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surveyed reproducibility features (empirical evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey of 50 RL papers (NeurIPS/ICML/ICLR 2018) checked presence of various reproducibility features and reported % yes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported percentages: Paper has experiments: 100%; Paper uses neural networks: 90%; All hyperparams for proposed algorithm provided: 90%; All hyperparams for baselines provided: 60%; Code is linked: 55%; Method for choosing hyperparams specified: 20%; Evaluations on some variation of a hold-out test set: 10%; Significance testing applied: 5%. Use these as empirical indicators of common (missing) practices and targets for improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalization evaluation: train/test separation and varied tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Generalization in RL: separate random seeds for train/test, separate tasks for train/test, use different image/video backgrounds, and evaluate on held-out tasks to measure generalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design evaluation protocols that test out-of-distribution generalization (different tasks/environments/backgrounds/seeds) rather than only re-testing on the training task.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report implementation and codebase details for baselines
rubrics_metrics.description: Codebase comparison (e.g., TRPO implementations) — document which implementation was used and differences between codebases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using baseline implementations, identify the repository/version and note implementation differences that could affect results; consider comparing multiple implementations to assess robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply and report statistical significance testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance testing applied (survey shows small fraction of papers do this).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform appropriate statistical tests and report p-values/confidence intervals or other inferential statistics to support claims of improvement.
